newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom NZ delivers few surprises in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Telecom NZ delivers few surprises in first quarter.

text.p: Telecom Corp of New Zealand on Tuesday delivered few surprises with a first quarter net profit of NZ$188 million (US$120 million), although a pledge to cut costs and capital expenditure over the next three years was greeted positively.
New Zealand's largest listed company grew earnings in the three months to June 30 by NZ$10.9 million, or 6.2 percent, from the NZ$177.1 million achieved in the same period last year.
Analysts, who had forecast a profit in the region of $190 million, said the result was in line with expectations.
"Revenues were more than what some people were expecting, but correspondingly the cost growth was a bit more, so the net effect was as expected," said one.
Telecom said first quarter revenues rose 7.0 percent on a normalised basis to NZ$800.6 million, while reported expenses grew by 14.6 percent to NZ$490.2 million.
Chief executive Roderick Deane said this level of cost growth was unacceptable, and announced new cost-cutting initiatives grouped under the heading Performance 2000.

He said the aim of the programme was to permanently remove a substantial amount from previously planned operating costs in Telecom's core business, and to cut NZ$500 million from previously planned capital expenditure over the next three years.
Guy Hallwright, analyst at First NZ Capital, said the focus on costs and capex was "clearly positive", but it was something the company had been talking about for some time.
"So it may well be that the market has factored in most, if not all of that," he said.
Deane said the benefits of Performance 2000 would start to be felt in the second half of this financial year, although the programme carried its own costs.
Asked if the initiative would result in a net gain on Telcom's bottomline in the second half, Deane said that was unclear.
"Certainly we'll see a slowdown in the rate of costs in the second half of this year and what happens to earnings will be dependent on what happens with revenues," he said.

Telecom was still feeling the impact of a flat economic environment, he said, but the revenue and growth rates achieved in the first quarter showed that telecommunications remained one of the strongest sectors of the economy.
"Telecom has continued to achieve growth in volumes and revenues significantly greater than the general level of economic activity," Deane said.
Normalised national call revenues rose just 1.6 percent and international call revenues fell 1.2 percent, but Enhanced Network Services and mobile revenues grew handsomely.

"Enhanced network services are an increasingly important part of Telecom's core business, generating 11.1 percent of total revenue in the first quarter, compared with just 9.2 percent in the first quarter of the previous year," Deane said.
He said cellular connections grew to 443,900 at the end of the first quarter, up 24.1 percent on the same period last year.
Cellular and other mobile services generated 11.8 percent of total revenue in the quarter, up from 10.4 percent last year.
Brokers said Telecom's profit result was viewed as neutral to slightly positive by the sharemarket, where the stock gained eight cents to NZ$7.60 on a rising bourse.
Bell Atlantic and Ameritech Corp each own a quarter of Telecom.
